title: Assessing your ancestry/DNA to hone in your diet
summary: NH explains how he shaped his diet around the diseases that run in his family (colon and prostate) by talking with male elders, with guidance from a longevity nutritionist, rather than genetic tests. He urges viewers to investigate what their relatives died of, protect their genetically weak organs, cut foods that disagree with them even subtly, and favor foods that slowly make them feel better.
claims: NH did not take a DNA test; he built his diet from family history by talking with male elders like his uncle, supervised by a longevity-focused nutritionist
Diet matters less than training for muscle building but is the number one factor for longevity and disease avoidance, more than cardio or lifting
What you eat every day compounds over time and dwarfs your training tonnage, yet most people eat mindlessly
Paying attention to diet can be the difference between dying in your 60s and in your 80s
Like genetic strong points in bodybuilding, everyone has genetically strong and weak organs; focus on protecting the weak organ that runs in your family because it will fail first
NH must limit liquid dairy (milk, yogurt), certain fish and red meat, which aggravate his family condition, and favors tomatoes, onions, garlic and small amounts of red wine
Colon and prostate disease kill every male in NH's family, and he considers himself next in line
The earlier you identify a hereditary disease risk, the more prevention you can do; men who catch conditions in their 40s-50s still gain 10 years
Ask your family what your relatives died of, on both the paternal and maternal lines, to learn which conditions you may be predisposed to
If no relative has seen a nutritionist, research your conditions online using credible sources; most conditions have aggravating and protective foods
Foods that improve most conditions tend to be vegetables; red meat rarely helps any condition
Nothing is wrong with animal products, but they should not make up the majority of your calories or food volume
Balancing protein, fats and carbs is easy; the hard part is filling those macros with foods that agree with you
If a food makes you sick, stop eating it; taking lactose pills to eat cheese only tricks the body
Some foods disagree with you without obvious symptoms: milk made NH retain water and fat in odd areas, and too much red meat showed similar quiet signs
Foods are negative, neutral or beneficial; beneficial foods slowly make you feel better and should be eaten in abundance
Eating tomatoes, onions and garlic daily changed how NH felt and his body composition dramatically
Detach emotionally from foods that taste good but do not do you good
Diet changes take a long time; it is a lifelong process and good diet choices stay with you even if you lose your muscle
Being muscular is pointless if you die in your 50s; health comes above bodybuilding
